decision.title: IR passes walk each body once, with a cheaper child walk (packet )

body.p: , after , , , , . No header changed; the IR after the passes is the same, item demands included.

item.p: Whom it serves: every compile, first large ones (EN 16931's Schematron and pre-compiled XSLT). Pays: two arrays lent across functions in the demand and fusion passes, two slot arrays per function in the demand pass, a byte per function in the fusion pass.

Profile (callgrind, release, base ae61af90e): validate --schematron of one invoice 1.613 x 10^9 instructions, the IR passes 0.502 of it (demand 0.200, descendant 0.074, fusion 0.066, hoist 0.064, filter-index 0.041, verify 0.030, global-read 0.028). No cost grew faster than the unit (the growth series of and doubled x 1.97 to 2.02 per doubling before and after); the constants were large. The unit (about 155,000 expressions) was walked about ten times: make_owners in five passes (0.135), a slot census per function in the descendant, demand and fusion passes (0.081), the demand members (0.061), a plain walk per function in fusion (0.020). Each step of a walk went through children_of into a local array, then pass_array_append, a call and a memcpy of a variable size per child: push_every_child cost about 130 instructions per expression. The demand pass also allocated its member arrays per function (230 functions, the largest with most of the unit) and, in each settling round, noted every member's reads again, looking up native function names with strlen.

Mechanism, no new machinery (src/ir_loop_passes.c): push_every_child switches on the kind and writes the indices in place, room made once per expression (pass_array_reserve; catch clauses, sort keys and merge streams in push_listed_children). The demand pass makes no owners: a function's body is a tree (the verifier's invariant), so a member is inside a STREAM or MERGE when its parent is one or is inside one, as make_owners marked it; the census is counted as the members are collected (one walk of the body), and a FILTER predicate's role, which needs the whole census, is decided after the walk. The descendant pass counts each function's census from the expressions owners gives it (grouped once, ), without a walk. The fusion pass finds the functions that hold a QUANTIFIED in one scan of owners (fusion only makes a QUANTIFIED of one). The demand pass notes the reads that do not depend on a member's demand once per function (all but a DOCUMENT_ORDER's), and each round adds the DOCUMENT_ORDER reads to them. The other passes' walks (hoist, filter-index, the owners of fusion and descendant) keep their place and gain from the cheaper step. Golden file: src/ir_verify.c.

Measured, instructions x 10^9 (callgrind, release; base ae61af90e and the change built alike from snapshots): invoice validate --schematron 1.613 to 1.413 (-12.4 %), the IR passes 0.502 to 0.302 (demand 0.200 to 0.100, descendant 0.074 to 0.042, fusion 0.066 to 0.028, hoist 0.064 to 0.047, filter-index 0.041 to 0.027, make_owners 0.135 for five to 0.057 for four); invoice transform 1.618 to 1.506 (-6.9 %), the passes 0.282 to 0.171; growth N = 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256: 0.553, 1.089, 2.163, 4.319, 8.681, 17.496 to 0.517, 1.018, 2.021, 4.034, 8.111, 16.355 (at N = 256 the passes 2.757 to 1.615, demand 0.939 to 0.442); templates of 6, 24, 96, 384 assertions 0.266, 0.956, 3.708, 14.719 to 0.249, 0.894, 3.467, 13.757; xmark-all 8.638 to 8.637. Processor seconds (interleaved, a shared 4-CPU machine; fastest of 15): validate 0.246 to 0.221, transform 0.214 to 0.202; fastest of 5: N = 128 1.190 to 1.137, N = 256 2.461 to 2.293, 384 assertions 2.063 to 1.906, xmark-all 1.002 to 1.007 (noise); the XT40 run (its 414,470 compiles and the transforms) 338.6 to 333.9. Outputs equal byte for byte on every run above.

Same result: the IR text form after the passes and a hash of every expression's item demand (which the text form does not show), dumped by a scratch-only hook in sxml_ir_run_passes, are identical on the EN 16931 .sch compile (286 MB of text), the EN 16931 XSLT (141 MB), the growth stylesheets, and all 414,470 units the XT40 suite compiles (a text hash and a demand hash per unit, in order). Conformance setup: base and change built alike (preset , snapshots of ae61af90e and of the change), run side by side on the same machine with TZ, LANG and LC_ALL unset, from each snapshot's root: sxml-qt4 run --spec=XP40 --format=json, sxml-qt4 run --spec=XQ40 --format=json, sxml-xslt-test run --format=json (default catalogs). XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114, XT40 12,185 passed in both: 0 outcomes differ, case by case (47,313, 47,313 and 13,867 cases). 7.30's suite through sxml-schematron-test run: 463 passed, 3 failed, 43 implementation-defined, 5 not applicable, as before; VEFA (run_vefa.py, the official UBL XSLT over the Invoice and CreditNote unit tests) 1,133 of 1,133. debug-gcc: 459 of 459 tests pass (kotlin/jvm and swift/linux skipped); clang-tidy clean on the file; tools/check-call-cycles.py finds no cycle ().

Left: on the invoice the passes are 21 % of validate --schematron: the demand pass 0.100 (its member walk with the census 0.061, of which growing the members array 0.014: the allocator zeroes each new block), make_owners 0.014 in each of four passes (each pass needs the owners of the unit as it starts it; keeping them across passes would need every pass to give owners to what it adds), the hoist pass's analyse_let 0.020, verify 0.030, global-read 0.028.
